highlights.title: Apple Pushes Back on DOJ Request for More Evidence
highlights.description: Apple and the U.S. Department of Justice disagree over how much newer evidence Apple must hand over in their antitrust case, according to a new court filing this week. The two sides previously agreed to a June 20, 2025 cutoff for Apple's records. With the evidence-gathering phase now scheduled to end in late May 2027, lawyers want Apple to supply documents created up to 30 days before that deadline. They say newer records could help establish whether the alleged anticompetitive practices are con

highlights.title: Nvidia's role as AI financier faces first big test as neoclouds take market hit
highlights.description: As Nvidia has gone from chipmaker to industry financier, some investors see the company taking on outsized risk tied to the AI buildout.

highlights.title: Turmoil hits AI buildout as neoclouds face pressure, credit risks mount and Solidigm pulls IPO
highlights.description: Stock slumps, pulled IPOs and rising spreads on credit default swaps this week sets stage for hyperscaler earnings.

highlights.title: Meta is delaying its controversial new business terms amid scraping concerns
highlights.description: Meta drew flak for an upcoming change to its business terms that would allow it to scrape business accounts' content for AI training.

highlights.title: Apple Closes French Stores Ahead of Further Protests
highlights.description: Seven Apple stores across France are closed on today, as the country prepares for another round of demonstrations a week after looters targeted two of the company's locations. As first spotted by MacGeneration, the affected stores include all three Paris locations: Champs-Élysées, Opéra, and Marché Saint-Germain. Apple's website also lists Saturday closures for Bordeaux Sainte-Catherine, Lille, Strasbourg, and Aix-en-Provence. The closures are likely a precaution to protect employees and stores

highlights.title: Using an Apple Pencil With the iPhone Duo: What to Know
highlights.description: The iPhone Duo is compatible with the Apple Pencil, if you have the right one. MacRumors videographer Dan Barbera tested the ‌Apple Pencil‌ with the ‌iPhone Duo‌ to see if it's a useful tool to pick up. If you already have an ‌Apple Pencil‌ 1, ‌Apple Pencil‌ 2, or ‌Apple Pencil‌ Pro to use with an iPad, you're going to be disappointed to hear they won't work with the ‌iPhone Duo‌. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ only works with the ‌Apple Pencil‌ with USB-C, which is $79 from Apple, but you can get it from Ama

highlights.title: Malaysia May Widen Ban on Israel-Based Waze Traffic App, PM Says
highlights.description: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s security cannot be compromised as he held fast on the government’s partial ban of Google’s navigation app Waze and said authorities aren’t ruling out even wider restrictions.

highlights.title: Russia deploys 3D-printed cruise missiles with US electronics in Ukraine, can hit 500mph with a 745-mile range
highlights.description: The Filin missile, which was deployed between late September and early October of this year, reportedly used 3D-printed and commercial parts to save on cost.

highlights.title: YouTuber escapes the modern AI tech market by recreating his 1996 PC
highlights.description: Exhaustion with tech market prompt Youtuber to remake their first PC — 1996 build fueled by nostalgia and AI weariness

highlights.title: Garmin Vivoactive 5 and Forerunner 165 Are up to 30 Percent Off (2026)
highlights.description: I’ve tested almost every Garmin watch—these entry-level favorites are steeply discounted right now.
